full_judgment:
3. Defendant Nos. 1-4 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement and denied the material allegations made in the plaint. Their case is that Basanta Kumar was not the Karta of their family as they have been living in separate mess before CS Operation and CS Record has been correctly prepared in their names. Their further case is that Basanta Kumar transferred some lands in favour of Haladhar, defendant No. 1 and Bharat by registered deeds dated 13-5-1944, 6-3-1945 and 5-3-1948. The defendants got possession in the land of these Khatians. Basanta Kumar transferred his share to Haladhar and Bharat before the alleged pattan in favour of the plaintiffs. Basanta Kumar did not settle any land in favour of the plaintiffs by way of pattan. The suit land recorded in the names of the plaintiffs was again corrected in favour of defendants after filing objection under section 19(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. So the suit is liable to be dismissed. The trial Court decreed the suit. The appellate Court reversed the judgment and decree of the trial court. The High Court Division made the Rule absolute. 

 8. On point of possession, the court of appeal below it appears, disbelieved the evidence of plaintiffs' witnesses after assigning cogent reasons and similarly believed the evidence of possession of defendants' witnesses after proper scrutiny, and after assigning cogent reason. The court of appeal below further held that the DWs stated that the suit land consisting of 14 plots are in possession of the defendant and the suit lands are near to the dwelling house of the defendants. On consideration of evidence of possession adduced by both parties the appellate Court below held that if we look into the oral evidence on record then we can rely upon the testimonies of the DWs, as they are independent witnesses. On the other hand, the PWs are tainted and shaky and, as such, they cannot be relied upon.
